title: Finite affine section cover in a single positive tensor power
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $L$ an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There exist $m>0$, $r\ge0$, and global section morphisms $s_i: \mathcal O_X\to L^{\otimes m}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], indexed by $\operatorname{ULift}(\operatorname{Fin}(r+1))$, such that each complement $X_{s_i}$ of the support of its zero locus is affine, and $\bigcup_iX_{s_i}=X$. The zero locus is the locally principal ideal generated by the coefficient of $s_i$ in a rank-one trivialization.

source.place: Morphisms Lemma 01VS, first paragraph (finite affine section cover, degrees made common); Properties Definition 01PS, with the local rank-one description of nonvanishing.

proof.text: Use ampleness to choose an affine nonvanishing positive-degree section locus around each point; quasi-compactness selects finitely many.

Take the product of the positive degrees and raise each section to the quotient power, using tensor exponent isomorphisms. In a local rank-one basis the new coefficient is a positive power of the old one, so the unit locus is unchanged.

Evaluation at one identifies section morphisms with global sections. In a rank-one stalk the germ is outside maximalIdeal times the module exactly when its coefficient is a unit, equivalently outside the support of the locally principal zero ideal. Enumerate the nonempty finite family; on an empty scheme use m=1 and one zero section with locus the empty affine open.
